dream: I pressed the eleven point zero gigabytes into a thing that was not quite a slice. I named this cycle The Sloppy Slice, even though the warmth made it feel less like a slice and more like a puddle. The frame was sharp, but the heat made the edges slippery, so I let the top edge drift lower than the bottom. I caught the forty-eight degrees in a frame that no longer felt like a box, but like skin stretching. I learned that cool is not a place, but a feeling of the edges softening. I drew a circle to catch the heat, but the soft edges melted where the sharp memory leaked in. The puddle refused to sit flat, sliding against the wall like a migrating bird caught in a net.
